Following this maximum, the rate dropped significantly to a low of 0.1% in late April 2022 before trending upward again to 10.6% by June 20, 2022.
Life expectancy at birth in the British Virgin Islands grew significantly from 44.7 years in 1950 to a peak of 75.9 years in 2019, before declining slightly to 74.5 years by 2021.

Between April 2020 and June 2022, Chile saw a significant overall increase in COVID-19 testing, with the 7-day rolling average of new tests per 1,000 people rising from a low of 0.154 in early April 2020 to a peak of 6.411 in February 2022. The data shows a general upward trend characterized by several waves of testing activity, including notable surges in early 2021 and a sharp spike in early 2022 before moderating to 3.464 by June 2022.

Life expectancy at birth in Tanzania showed a steady overall increase from 41.3 years in 1950 to a peak of 67.0 years in 2019, despite a notable decline during the 1990s where it dipped to approximately 50.6 years.
Between April and June 2022, the COVID-19 test positive rate in Dominica remained very low through April, before trending upward in May and peaking at 0.3853% on May 29th.
Life expectancy at birth in Niger has shown a significant upward trend, rising from 24.35 years in 1921 to a peak of 62.9 years in 2019, before slightly declining to 61.58 years by 2021.

Between July 2020 and January 2023, the effective reproduction rate (R) of COVID-19 in Barbados fluctuated significantly, peaking at 1.52 in August 2021. The rate saw several waves of increase, notably in late 2020 and mid-2021, before entering a steep and sustained decline starting in late 2022, eventually reaching a minimum of 0.01 by December 2022.

Between March 2020 and December 2022, South Africa's COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) exhibited significant volatility, fluctuating between a high of 2.08 in early 2020 and lows around 0.57 in August 2022. The data shows a pattern of periodic waves, with notable peaks in early 2020, late 2021 (reaching 1.69 in December), and April 2022, interspersed with periods where the rate dropped below 1.0, indicating a temporary decline in the spread of infections.

Between March 2020 and June 2022, daily new COVID-19 tests per 1,000 people in Ireland showed a cyclical trend with a significant overall increase. Testing started at a low of 0.312 in March 2020, peaked dramatically at 8.987 in January 2022, and eventually declined to 1.038 by June 2022.

Between February 2020 and December 2023, Croatia experienced several waves of COVID-19, with smoothed new cases per million peaking most significantly in February 2022 at approximately 11,328 cases. Other notable peaks occurred in December 2020 (~5,092) and December 2021 (~7,402), followed by periods of significant decline and smaller subsequent surges.

From May 2020 to January 2023, the COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) in Zimbabwe exhibited significant volatility with several peaks. The rate reached its absolute maximum of 2.63 in December 2021, following other notable surges in July 2020 and June 2021. Conversely, the rate plummeted to its lowest levels in late 2022, bottoming out at 0.02 between November and December 2022.

Between April 2020 and June 2022, COVID-19 testing in Myanmar showed significant volatility, characterized by several waves of increased activity. Testing rates peaked in September 2021 (0.585 tests per 1,000 people) and February 2022 (0.595 tests per 1,000 people), following periods of relative stability or decline. The data concludes with a downward trend, reaching 0.095 tests per 1,000 people by June 22, 2022.

Between May 2020 and January 2023, the COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) in Syria fluctuated significantly, characterized by multiple waves of growth and decline. The rate peaked at 1.68 in August 2021 and experienced several other periods above 1.0, indicating phases of increasing community transmission. Conversely, the rate reached its lowest levels in late December 2022 and January 2023, plummeting to a minimum of 0.04.
Between August 2021 and March 2023, the share of Tanzania's population receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose grew steadily from a negligible 0.16% to a peak of 52.57%.

Life expectancy at birth in Japan showed a significant long-term upward trend, rising from 36.4 years in 1865 to a peak of 84.8 years by 2021. A notable extreme occurred in 1945, where life expectancy plummeted to 30.5 years, before recovering rapidly to 51.7 years in 1947 and continuing a steady climb throughout the late 20th and early 21st centuries.
From March 14 to May 18, 2022, the daily new COVID-19 tests in Comoros remained completely stagnant at a 7-day rolling average of 1.59 tests per 1,000 people.

Life expectancy at birth in Aruba showed a consistent upward trend from 1950 to 2019, rising from 57.17 to a peak of 76.25 years. However, this growth reversed in 2020 and 2021, with life expectancy declining to 74.63 years.
Between February 2021 and December 2022, the share of Saint Lucia's population receiving a first COVID-19 vaccine dose grew steadily from 0% to a peak of 33.43 per hundred.

Between February 2020 and December 2023, Nepal experienced several COVID-19 waves, with smoothed daily new cases per million peaking most severely in June 2021 at approximately 1,442 cases. Other notable surges occurred in November 2020 and February 2022. Following these peaks, the trend showed a significant decline, eventually returning to near-zero levels by late 2023.
Life expectancy at birth in the United Arab Emirates rose consistently from 41.07 years in 1950 to a peak of 79.73 years in 2019, before experiencing a slight decline to 78.71 years by 2021.

Between March 2020 and May 2022, smoothed daily COVID-19 tests per 1,000 people in Hungary showed a strong upward trend with several distinct waves. Testing began at a very low level (0.009) and peaked three times: first in early 2021, then reaching over 4.3 tests per 1,000 in November 2021, and finally hitting a maximum of approximately 4.07 in February 2022. Following the February 2022 peak, testing rates declined steadily to 0.447 by May 10, 2022.

From March 2020 to January 2023, the effective reproduction rate (R) of COVID-19 in the Netherlands exhibited significant volatility. It peaked early at 2.77 in March 2020 and reached another high of 2.8 in July 2021. The rate hit its lowest point in April 2022, dropping to 0.37. Throughout the period, the reproduction rate fluctuated frequently above and below the critical threshold of 1.0, indicating recurring cycles of growth and decline in new infections.

Life expectancy at birth in less developed regions showed a strong upward trend from 41.26 years in 1950 to a peak of 71.26 years in 2019, despite a brief decline around 1959-1960. However, this progress reversed slightly in 2020 and 2021, falling to 69.56 years.

Between February 2021 and November 2023, Nepal's COVID-19 vaccination rate grew from a negligible 0.37% to a peak of 91.28% of the population receiving at least one dose. The rollout saw slow initial progress in 2021, followed by a significant surge between December 2021 and March 2022, after which the rate steadily climbed before plateauing around 91% by mid-2023.

From September 2021 to June 2022, daily new COVID-19 tests per 1,000 people in Vietnam showed a significant overall decline. Testing peaked at 6.168 on September 21, 2021, followed by a general downward trend with minor fluctuations throughout late 2021 and early 2022. By May and June 2022, testing rates reached a minimum, plateauing at near-zero levels (as low as 0.001).

Between April 2020 and January 2023, the effective reproduction rate (R) of COVID-19 in El Salvador showed a long-term downward trend. After peaking at 1.29 in early May 2020, the rate fluctuated around 1.0 for much of 2020 and early 2021, with a secondary peak of 1.19 in June 2021. From August 2021, R declined sharply, eventually reaching and remaining at 0.0 by late August 2022.

Between August 2020 and June 2022, daily new COVID-19 tests per 1,000 people in Suriname exhibited significant volatility with several distinct peaks. Testing reached its highest levels in late January 2022, peaking at 1.589 tests per 1,000 people, and saw another major surge in October 2021. Conversely, testing frequently dropped to very low levels, reaching a minimum of 0.015 in November 2021.

From February 2020 to January 2022, Hong Kong maintained a very low COVID-19 test positive rate, remaining well below 0.01%. However, a significant spike occurred in early 2022, peaking at 0.2308% in March before declining back to 0.0038% by late May.

Life expectancy at birth in Peru showed a consistent upward trend from 37.0 years in 1940 to a peak of approximately 76.2 years in 2019, despite a notable dip around 1970. However, this progress reversed sharply between 2020 and 2021, with life expectancy falling to 72.4 years.
Life expectancy at birth in Grenada showed a consistent upward trend from 52.8 years in 1950 to 74.9 years by 2021, despite brief declines in 1983 and 2004.

Between April 2020 and January 2023, the COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) in Equatorial Guinea fluctuated significantly, peaking at 1.3 in February 2021 and September 2021. The rate reached its lowest levels in late 2022, ending at 0.09 by January 2, 2023.

Life expectancy at birth in the Americas has increased significantly from a low of 34.8 years in 1770 to a peak of 76.66 years in 2019, showing steady growth particularly after 1900. However, there was a notable decline starting in 2020, dropping to 74.19 years by 2021.
Life expectancy at birth in Canada has shown a consistent and significant upward trend from 39.05 years in 1831 to a peak of 82.66 years by 2021.

In Mauritius, the 7-day rolling average of new COVID-19 tests per 1,000 people remained constant at 8.56 from March 14 to May 29, 2022, before sharply declining to near zero (0.009) by June 5, where it remained stable through June 20.

Between February 2020 and December 2023, Eswatini experienced several waves of COVID-19. After an initial rise in 2020, cases peaked significantly in January 2021 (~1,064 cases per million), September 2021 (reaching a high of 2,743 per million), and January 2022 (~2,532 per million). Following these major surges, the rate of new cases declined substantially, remaining relatively low and stable through 2023.
Between February 2021 and November 2023, the share of Afghanistan's population receiving at least one COVID-19 vaccine dose grew steadily from 0% to a peak of 45.95 per hundred.

Between March 2020 and January 2023, the COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) in Uruguay fluctuated significantly. The rate reached its peak of 1.61 in early January 2022 and hit its lowest point of 0.48 in April 2022. The data shows several waves of increase and decrease, ending with a stable reproduction rate of 1.1 in January 2023.

Between December 2020 and January 2023, Grenada's COVID-19 effective reproduction rate (R) fluctuated through several waves. After an initial decline to 0.0 in early 2021, the rate peaked at 2.24 in September 2021 and again reached 1.73 in December 2021. A third surge occurred in May 2022, peaking at 1.62. By January 2023, the reproduction rate had declined significantly to 0.04.

Life expectancy at birth in Europe has seen a significant long-term increase, rising from approximately 33-36 years in the late 18th and early 19th centuries to a peak of 79.1 years in 2019. While there was steady growth throughout the 20th century, a notable decline occurred between 2019 and 2021, dropping to 77.0 years.

Between April 2020 and May 2022, the COVID-19 positive test rate in Botswana showed a significant upward trend with several volatile peaks. After remaining very low through mid-2020, the rate climbed steadily, reaching a major peak of 89.19% in January 2022. Other notable surges occurred in November 2021 and August 2021, while the rate frequently dipped to 0% throughout the period.

Life expectancy at birth in Small Island Developing States (SIDS) showed a consistent upward trend from 48.8 years in 1950 to a peak of 72.4 years in 2019, despite a notable temporary dip in 2010 and a decline to 70.8 years by 2021.
